content.text: I've verified the load-bearing claims directly. Scoring now.

scores.evidence:
OBSERVED REJECTION RATE ≈ 0 across the whole corpus history. 0 of 18 features carry `status: returned` (grep over features/*.md: 10 assigned, 8 delivered, 0 returned). 0 of 16 initiatives were rejected. I grepped every co-occurrence of a rejection verb (fail|reject|return|blocked|removed) within 120 characters of any of the nine principle slugs across features/, requests/, decisions/, sessions/, initiatives/ and basis/: six hits total, and on inspection NOT ONE is a rejection — they are add-usability run notes (feat-implementation-good.md:151), a designer-criteria row (feat-tool-skills-rest.md:587), two initiative-check attach rows, a PO self-check row, and a 2026-08-23 rationale repair. No check verdict anywhere cites a principle clause as the reason an artifact was turned away.

HYPOTHETICAL REJECTION RATE is also low for most of the set because the obligations are procedural, not discriminating. Against the last ~20 delivered artifacts, `no-orphan-activities`, `single-source-of-truth`, `use-defined-terms` and `governed-context` would reject almost none (all were authored inside a defined process, with one home, using glossary terms). The two that would reject at Spool's two-thirds benchmark are `tools-through-skills` (0 of 25 process definitions reference artifact_tools.py while 71 bare sed/grep/awk/cut/head/tail invocations sit in their own run: blocks — I counted sed 21, cut 20, grep 12, head 10, awk 8, tail 6) and `define-good-up-front`'s different-role clause (feature-authoring runs draft and self-check both as lead-po; adr-authoring runs author and record both as the architect). Both would reject the majority of recent work and rejected none of it.

CONTESTABILITY: ~3 of 9 contested, 6 permission-to-play. Negations no competent shop holds: "activities may sit outside any process", "a fact may have several authoritative homes", "a definition need not be findable", "load context from unapproved sources". Genuinely contested: `tools-through-skills` (many shops prefer bare CLI over a skill wrapper), `least-context` (contested against full-context approaches), `define-good-up-front`'s separate-role check (contested by pair/self-review practice). The corpus's own Lencioni screen row states a position for exactly one column — define-good-up-front, "pass — most systems do NOT work this way"; the other eight read a bare "pass" with no position written.

CHEAP PROXIES: trade-off language across all three sets totals 3 + 4 + 4 instances of "rather than"/"instead of", all incidental clause connectives, none a named accepted cost. Obligations per principle (MUST bullets, counted per heading in basis/principles.md): define-good-up-front 5, tools-through-skills 4, least-context 3, feedback-loops-with-consumers 3, and 2 each for the remaining five — 26 stands under 9 names. Rationales with a concrete failure example: all carry one, but by rule it must be GENERIC.

STRUCTURAL HAZARD CONFIRMED VERBATIM: basis/fitness/principle-set.fitness.md Scenario 3 requires each rationale to "reference no operational history of the product — artifacts, issues, incidents, decision records, or counts." That forbids exactly the evidence Spool's Test #1 demands. No principle in this corpus can prove it came from research, by rule.
scores.counter_evidence: Real and worth stating. (1) The fitness SETS have genuine rejection power even though the principles don't: basis/principles.md v4 history records cold read round 3 returning "external-standards-first rationale lacked its generic failure example (scenario 3 fail)", and v5 is the forced repair — a check that failed something and changed the text. Four screen rounds ran on that one document. (2) The authority exercised rejection power on a principle itself: `delivery-verified` was removed whole on 2026-09-15 with the reason recorded in his words — "There is no mechanism that would be possible to implement in the current system that would meet the principle." A rule in force was deleted, which most rule-making systems never manage. (3) `tools-through-skills` and `single-source-of-truth` did produce filed findings (lead-ng3hc, lead-qd0an, lead-jzmz5) — the principles name defects accurately after the fact, they just never stop anything before it. (4) Complication against a clean zero: the delivery-verified removal was followed two days later by `effect-shown` in basis/implementation-principles.md, near-identical in substance, with no record connecting the two — so even the one clear rejection did not hold.

scores.factor_name: Check economics: does each check pay, and is its verdict reproducible?
scores.evidence:
CHECK MASS IS NOT THE PROBLEM — I counted it myself. 207 steps across 25 process definitions; 25 step ids contain check/screen/verify/judge/review = 12%. 14 of 25 processes have no check step at all. The largest single definition, request-intake (6,562 words, 22 steps), has zero. "Every process ends in a check" is false at the step level.

CHECK COST IS THE PROBLEM. 279 of 592 subagent runs (47%) carry a check/screen/review description and consume 2,173,552 of 5,355,852 subagent output tokens (41%). The authority's own read of init-request-routing: 136 agent-minutes, 66 first implementation, 70 review cycles — 51% of run time — and 20 screen rounds on 8 artifacts. 60 work items ran numbered screen rounds; 32 reached round 3 and 7 reached round 4.

DEFECT FRACTION, JUDGED CHECK: cold-reviewer returned "findings" on 71 of 78 runs and "clean" on 2 — p ≈ 0.91. By Deming's kp that station is worth inspecting. But the output is mostly undecidable: 242 of 381 findings (65%) are "wobbly" — the judge could not decide — and 135 (35%) cite criterion `uncovered`, defined in basis/types/screen-review.md:26 as "for a defect no criterion names." A third of all findings cannot cite the clause they enforce, by design. The shop's own 2026-09-05 analysis: "the cap, not convergence, ended every screen" on seven of eight artifacts, and "the check became where quality is produced."

DEFECT FRACTION, SELF-SCREEN: the opposite extreme and pro forma by construction. I counted the pass cells: 48 in basis/principles.md, 47 in implementation-principles.md, 40 in experience-principles.md, 33 in architecture-principles.md = 168 passes, 0 fail verdicts corpus-wide (the "fail" string hits are prose inside the compile-mapping table, not cells). 100% historical pass rate, asserted by the author in the same pass that wrote the text.

REPRODUCIBILITY — the corpus answers this itself and the answer is 0 of 3. basis/principles.md §Accepted tradeoffs, verbatim: "**The two judged screen rows below claim passes for those principles that the judge could not reproduce.** Accepted, and recorded here rather than silently." Three independent cold screens of three different sets all failed fitness scenario 5 ("every claimed pass is one the judge can reproduce") the same way: lead-zddhu on principles.md, lead-fstd0 on architecture-principles.md, lead-u0ow4 on implementation-principles.md (2026-09-17, filed as "Third instance of one class"). Agreement rate between the author's asserted pass and an independent judge: zero, three for three.

ESCAPE COST: the check has never caught the thing that mattered. 0 of 18 features returned; the P0 that shipped (lead-ibme0 — a feature assigned with an unrecorded decision, silently) was caught by a human reading a line by hand, not by any check step.
scores.counter_evidence: Substantial, and it is the most important counter-evidence in this analysis. (1) THE MECHANICAL CHECKS ARE PERFECTLY REPRODUCIBLE AND ALL PASS. I ran them: `python3 basis/tools/lint_basis.py` → PASS, 0 violations; `compile_role.py --check` → ok on all 9 roles; compile_principles output byte-identical to the compiled block; 25 of 25 process skills match their load point. Every check a machine performs is reproducible; every check a reader performs is not. (2) THE COLD SCREEN IS THE ONE CHECK WITH A REAL DETECTION RECORD — 6 defects, including the three that indict the self-screen it competes with. lead-u0ow4 states the mechanism outright: "the screen table is written by the same agent whose text it scores, in the same pass, and nothing re-derives a claimed pass... The cold-reviewer screen-read step is what actually catches this, every time." (3) A literal mechanical instruction inside a judged scenario converts it into a reproducible check: implementation-guidance fitness scenario 6 says "Count the document's words... State the count and pass/fail", and guidance records are the ONLY artifact class near its word target (median 1.1x, 7/12 over, against 2.4x–4.3x everywhere else) because makers actually ran `wc -w`. (4) The shop already removed three of the four check-shaped processes on 2026-09-08 — it acted on this diagnosis before the authority raised it.

scores.factor_name: Flow efficiency, the single-human constraint, and batch size
scores.evidence:
GOVERNANCE VARIANT IS RED BY A LARGE MARGIN. Of every token the shop's own instrument ever recorded (2,716,421 across 44 rows in 7 files): coordinate/route 64.4%, discovery dialogue 19.6%, MAKE 11.5%, check 4.5%. By role: router 1,247,751 + lead-pm 1,034,027 = 84% to coordination; the three making roles 434,643 = 16%. Time spent satisfying the process about the item exceeds time on the item by roughly five to one.

FLOW EFFICIENCY, 5 items end to end: 13 of the 15 features authored 09-02→09-09 went bet→assigned in 0–1 days — but that measures a markdown corpus editing itself, and the distribution does not survive contact with a build. init-implementation-process was bet 2026-09-09; its two features were authored 09-15 and 09-17 and neither has been built — 8 days open with no closed tail. Git log confirms the stall: 14 commits on 09-09, 1 on 09-10, then five consecutive zero-commit days (09-11 through 09-14), 6 on 09-15.

THE CONSTRAINT IS HANDOFF COUNT, NOT THE HUMAN. Only 10 of 207 steps are human (4.8%), 7 the authority's; product-flow v7 deliberately removed every human step after the bet. Median human turnaround is 6.9 minutes and 18% of his turns are one word. Yet 134 hours of wall-clock waited on the human against 43 hours of agent-active time — 3.11:1, produced by 258 handoffs, not by slow answers. The full flow is "21 agent runs and six human decides to reach one build" (shop's own 09-08 analysis).

THE REAL QUEUE HAS NO SERVER AT ALL. 13 of 41 requests (32%) are stalled — I verified the 7 `routed`-and-never-acted: operational-contract (09-04), step-communication (09-05), migration-review (09-06), messaging-invocations (09-07), initiative-cost-rollup (09-08), cost-per-execution (09-09), artifact-tools-round-trip (09-09). step-communication is named "awaiting the authority's answer" in 8 consecutive session records and is still `routed` today. 36 of 38 correction beads are open; 0 of the 19 filed since 09-06 have closed; 206 pre-rebaseline register items were open on 08-21 and all 206 are still open. Cause verified in the definitions: process definitions contain 8 `bd create`, 11 `bd close`, 3 `bd comment` and ZERO `bd list/show/query`. No defined activity ever reads the register. 28 of 34 open defects wait on nobody — this is an open loop, not a queue.

CLARIFICATION SHARE IS NOT FALLING. Per-initiative cost rose roughly nine-fold (7M cache-read tokens for the first, 64M for each of the last three) across four explicit efficiency interventions. Like-for-like feature-authoring: 192,791 tokens / 8.6 min on 09-09 → 241,852 / 15.4 min on 09-16, same four steps, same roles (+25% tokens, +79% minutes).

BATCH SIZE AND EXTERNAL VALIDATION: the product flow was approved end to end in one batch under brief-032. The interval to external validation is unbounded — no initiative has ever reached `completed` (13 active, 2 planned, 1 proposed, 0 completed), because the only writer of `completed` is reconcile-and-close, which the freeze bars from running. The system cannot observe its own throughput.

AUTHORITY SELF-REPORT — the outcome variable, and it moved the wrong way: cost/speed raised on 11 distinct days starting day 3; 2026-09-07 "We need drastically higher efficiency"; 2026-09-17 "This has been really slow to get moving."
scores.counter_evidence: (1) The small-change lane genuinely achieves flow: 20 of 41 requests routed to it, 28 requests `done`, and three changes taken to verified results in about 14 agent-minutes total — against ~4 hours and 136 agent-minutes for one full-flow initiative. Same agents, same corpus, same day. The shop diagnosed why itself: "no bet, no check of record, one screen only where a definition's own process requires it." (2) The structural move on the constraint was correct: product-flow v7 removed every human step after the bet, and 6 steps carry `asks` as held-and-resumed with defaults rather than as gates. (3) The single-review-cycle ruling of 09-05 did move mean max screen rounds from 2.74 to 2.23. (4) Dollar cost is genuinely not the constraint — a 15-feature product at the unimproved rate is a few hundred dollars of tokens. Steering the system at cost rather than at elapsed time pointed it at its cheapest resource.

scores.factor_name: Ceremonial mass: definitions never executed, rules never retired
scores.evidence:
NEVER-RUN SHARE: 7 of 25 process definitions have no recorded end-to-end execution — corpus-close-out, definition-chain-migration, reconcile-and-close, work-conversation, review-sweep, interaction-conformance-check, implementation. interaction-conformance-check (1,920 words, `status: approved`, rendered to .claude/skills/ and loadable) appears in ZERO session records. That is 28% never-run; but several more are unexecutable by construction while the shop is frozen (implementation, scenario-assignment's dispatch half, reconcile-and-close, the bc-emit and mailbox paths), pushing the unexecutable share past the 40% red flag. product-flow's entire second half has no receiver: no Bounded Context exists on this branch, and scenario-assignment's lead-shop-internal path is bead lead-ki66p, open since 2026-09-02 and worked around eleven times.

DEFINITION-TO-EXECUTION LAG, worst case: basis/processes/implementation.md and basis/implementation-principles.md were both authored 2026-09-17 — day 26 — and both stand `status: draft`. The definition of how to build software arrives on the last day of the window, unapproved, with zero executions. The 4,461 lines of Python that do exist have no tests (`git ls-files | grep -i test` returns nothing).

AUTHORED-AND-KILLED INSIDE 16 DAYS: 8,479 words of process definition (initiative-check 3,548, po-output-check 2,436, stakeholder-presentation 1,476, backlog-ordering 1,019) = 13.5% of the process corpus, retired 2026-09-08.

RETIREMENT WITHOUT SWEEP — the decisive finding, verified by grep. The four retirements happened in the source and nowhere else: po-output-check is still referenced in 19 files, initiative-check in 9, stakeholder-presentation in 8, backlog-ordering in 5. Worst instance: .claude/shop/primer.md, last committed 2026-08-31 (git log confirms — 17 days stale), loaded verbatim into EVERY session, names initiative-check / backlog-ordering / po-output-check as the live product flow and states "deliveries to the authority longer than ~300 words go through the `stakeholder-presentation` process — no exceptions" — a retired process with no replacement. It is in this session's own context. lint_basis.py passes clean over all of it because its link check verifies that a file resolves, never that its target is live. The corpus recorded the consequence: sess-2026-09-16-a, "the stale rendering was teaching the removal's opposite while the removal was being made." A retirement that leaves the compiled context teaching the retired rule is worse than no retirement.

ALSO UNSWEPT: lead-tmahe — backlog-ordering is `status: approved` and its check step routes into po-output-check, which is retired; unnoticed because product-flow no longer calls it at all. An approved process routing into a retired one.

BOZEMAN TEST on the obligations I could trace: I could not find one obligation that PREVENTED a concrete failure in the last 30 days. `single-source-of-truth` and `tools-through-skills` both named defects after they occurred (lead-qd0an — a two-homes breach stale 22 days undetected; lead-ng3hc — six artifact-tool gaps each worked around with sed/grep/cat, "including by the lead-pm role, which is the behaviour tools-through-skills forbids"). Red-tape share on that sample is high: the rules diagnose, they do not stop.
scores.counter_evidence: Genuinely better than the null trajectory on retirement, and this matters for the restart decision. (1) The retirement ratio is NOT zero: four process definitions retired 2026-09-08 in a deliberate flow simplification, and `delivery-verified` — a principle in force — was removed whole from basis/principles.md v12 on 2026-09-15 on the authority's word. March/Schulz/Zhou's expected trajectory is monotonic rule growth; this shop has deleted both a process layer and a standing principle inside 26 days. It CAN retire. What it cannot do is sweep the references. (2) Churn shows rules are genuinely revisited, not silted: 1,217 recorded revisions across 241 versioned documents, mean v5.0, with basis/principles.md at v12, the feature typedef at v18 and the glossary at v27 in 26 days. Rule half-life is days, not years. (3) The rendering machinery correctly REMOVED the retired processes' skills from the agent load point — the compilers swept what they owned. Every stale artifact I found is one no compiler owns.

scores.evidence:
I put each named source's own criteria against the corpus's rendering. Adopted intact: 3. Narrowed, inverted or dropped with NO recorded justification: 7.

TOGAF — five set-level criteria are Understandable, Robust, Complete, Consistent, Stable. All four principle sets render exactly three: "testable (TOGAF... understandable, complete, consistent)" (basis/principles.md:36, architecture:63, implementation:86, experience:69). **Robust and Stable DROPPED** — grep for either across basis/artifacts/principle-set.md, basis/guidelines/principle-set.md and basis/principles.md returns nothing but false positives; no justification recorded anywhere. Worse, **Consistent is INVERTED**: TOGAF's Consistent means the set allows a balance of interpretations without self-contradiction; the corpus folds it into a binary-testability criterion, which removes the balance of interpretations the source criterion exists to protect. ADOPTED INTACT: the Name/Statement/Rationale/Implications form (cited at basis/artifacts/principle-set.md:79) and the 10–20 count heuristic (9 working, 6 each elsewhere).

SPOOL — **Test #1 (comes from research) is INVERTED, in writing.** basis/fitness/principle-set.fitness.md Scenario 3 requires each rationale to "reference no operational history of the product — artifacts, issues, incidents, decision records, or counts." The corpus forbids by rule the only evidence Spool's first test accepts. No recorded justification. Test #2 (helps you say no) adopted in form as a screen row, but scored as the author's own one-line claim. **Test #4 (reversibility) appears only fused into Lencioni's row** via Scenario 6 ("the opposite rule is one an honest shop could adopt") — partially adopted, unattributed, and the remaining Spool tests do not appear.

LENCIONI — four value types (core, aspirational, permission-to-play, accidental). Only permission-to-play survives, as one screen row. Three dropped, unjustified.

BCP 14 — keyword vocabulary adopted by name in five documents and MANDATED by basis/artifacts/principle-set.md:59 ("MUST/SHOULD/MAY per BCP 14 — and is yes/no testable"). **RFC 2119 §6's necessity limit is DROPPED**: grep across all of basis/ for "sparingly" or "only be used where" returns zero hits. §6 says imperatives "MUST only be used where it is actually required... must not be used to try to impose a particular method on implementors" — and "The check MUST sit with a different role holding a different accountability" is precisely a method mandate. The discretion half is unused in practice: 263 MUST + 49 MUST NOT against 10 SHOULD, 0 SHOULD NOT and 26 MAY — 89.6% mandatory, and every SHOULD in the four principle sets is the boilerplate sentence defining the keyword, not a use.

RUMELT — "directs without prescribing method" adopted as a screen row. **The kernel's diagnosis-before-guiding-policy requirement is absent**: no principle set carries a diagnosis section, and Scenario 3's ban on operational history makes one impossible to write.

THE HOME-GROWN CRITERION, flagged hardest as the factor asks: "it implies at least one practice and one check" (basis/principles.md:42, repeated in all four sets and carried as a MANDATORY fitness-screen row). It has NO external parent — it is in none of TOGAF, Spool, Lencioni, Rumelt or BCP 14. And basis/artifacts/definition.md §Required sections 2 makes it structural for every definition in the corpus: "A closing **checks section** (its heading contains 'check') — every definition implies at least one check; a definition no check can cite does not govern anything", inherited by 10 of 24 typedefs. This is the clause that converts a principle set into a generator of process mass, and under the corpus's own `external-standards-first` ("Bespoke structure MUST be justified by a recorded gap in the form it rejects") it required a recorded gap. None exists.
scores.counter_evidence: Real credit due. (1) Every source is NAMED, in every set's Sources line and in the typedef's §Sources, with full citations after the 2026-08-23 close-out polish — most corpora that borrow TOGAF's form do not say so. The departures were findable precisely because the adoptions are declared. (2) One narrowing IS recorded honestly and precisely: Gherkin is adopted as "the readable G/W/T frame — syntax only, no interpreter" in basis/fitness/principle-set.fitness.md §Sources, with the boundary stated rather than assumed. That is exactly the discipline external-standards-first asks for, so the shop knows how to do it. (3) The corpus's own tension between TOGAF (whose principles are guidance) and BCP 14 (whose purpose is removing discretion) is the sharpest fidelity failure, and it is a sophisticated error, not a careless one — it comes from honouring external-standards-first twice without noticing the two standards pull opposite ways.

scores.evidence:
FINDABILITY FAILS ON THE MOST-ASKED QUESTION. "What is the current product flow?" requires reconciling at least three documents at conflicting states: .claude/shop/primer.md (always resident, names three retired processes as the live stages), basis/processes/product-flow.md v7 (current), and the 19/9/8/5 files still citing po-output-check / initiative-check / stakeholder-presentation / backlog-ordering. "Where is the bet taken?" has two live answers: basis/artifacts/initiative.md says "Bet directly at discovery... no separate check between framing and bet"; initiative-check.md still defines step `decide` — "Take the bet" — and is cited by the glossary, the initiative guideline and the initiative fitness set, all approved. "How long may an initiative be?" has two: initiative.md "At most 500 words" vs base-writing-style's target table "Initiative | 400".

STALENESS, MEASURED MECHANICALLY as the factor requires — this is the sharpest number I produced. I ran `compile_typedef.py --check` over all 24 artifact typedefs: **2 pass, 19 will-not-compile ("no `## Writing rules` section" — a section the artifact-typedef typedef declares required), 1 DIVERGED (implementation-guidance: both the guideline the maker reads and the fitness set the checker reads no longer match the typedef they are generated from), 2 refused (superseded/draft).** Only 6 of 30 files in basis/guidelines and basis/fitness carry `generated: true`. And `python3 basis/tools/lint_basis.py` returns "PASS: 0 violation(s)" over every bit of it — I read its checks: frontmatter fields, Document History position, duplicate `defines`, broken links, required headings, $ref sources, request/brief/guidance field shapes. No word count, no currency check, no check that a referenced definition is still approved.

DECODE COST PER SENTENCE rose as length fell: defined-term uses per 1,000 words went request-intake (09-04) 71.9 → product-flow (09-08) 86.7 → implementation (09-17) 94.2 — roughly one defined term every 11 words in the newest definition, against base-writing-style's own 24.3. A writer must hold 120 defined terms (82 glossary + 24 typedefs + 14 data types) and `use-defined-terms` obliges reaching for one wherever one fits.

THE (b)/(c)/(d) SHARE IS THE COST. Document History is 27% of the entire corpus — 1,520 rows, mean 76 words against a 25-word target, max 1,672 words in a single markdown table cell; 69% of all initiative words and 44% of all feature words. Cross-document verbatim repetition (12-word shingles, generated files excluded) is 16.9% of hand-written body words, worst in backlog orders at 54.9% where each day's order restates its predecessor. And 84.5% of a process definition never reaches any agent — 9,145 prompt words of 59,148, with product-flow at 2.7%.
scores.counter_evidence: Two findings genuinely contradict the "dense and unfindable" reading, and I tested both rather than taking them on report. (1) THE GLOSSARY IS HEALTHY. I ran every one of the 82 glossary terms against the whole basis tree, excluding its own definition: only 7 have fewer than 3 uses (simple type, rewrite-forward, conversation type, review record, action table, branched conversation, architecture decision record). 75 of 82 are load-bearing. By the factor's own deletion test, the glossary is in better shape than most production corpora. (2) THE TEXT AGENTS ACTUALLY READ IS THE PLAINEST TEXT IN THE CORPUS. Process step prompts — the only process text that enters an agent's context — measure 22.3 words per unit, 11.8% over 40 words, 31.1% stacking two or more qualifiers: LESS dense on every axis than the typedefs (33.5% stacking), the features (53.2%), or the rendered skills (52.5%). Median sentence length across process definitions is 14 words, typedefs 11, roles 10 — ordinary technical-writing numbers. So the runtime decode cost is low and the maintainer decode cost is high, which inverts the usual causal story: if agents interpret rules inconsistently, prose verbosity is not the channel, because the verbose material never reaches them. (3) The one place density IS extreme is the compilation step, and it is deliberate: 4,053 words of principle carrying 26 obligations become the 537-word always-resident block at one MUST per 21 words, with rationale, implications and screen stripped by design. The corpus solved its verbosity problem by deleting the interpretable half.

input.root_causes:
Three causes explain every failing factor. They are independent; fixing the writing fixes none of them.

**RC1 — Nothing in the system reads what the system writes. Every feedback channel terminates in a write.**
I verified this in the definitions, not just the outcomes: across all 25 process definitions there are 8 `bd create`, 11 `bd close` and 3 `bd comment` calls, and ZERO `bd list/show/query`. No defined activity ever reads the work register. The consequences are the factor scores: 36 of 38 correction beads open, 0 of the 19 filed since 2026-09-06 closed, 206 pre-rebaseline items open on 2026-08-21 and all 206 still open 26 days later; 7 requests `routed` and never acted on, one named "awaiting the authority's answer" in 8 consecutive session records; 7 cost files for 22 sessions with 2 empty including the newest. 28 of 34 open defects wait on nobody — this is not a bottleneck, it is an open loop, and "bottleneck" (H5) is the wrong model for it. The same shape explains ceremonial-mass: retirement happened in the sources on 2026-09-08 and nowhere else, because no activity re-reads the corpus as a whole — hence 19 files still citing po-output-check and a primer 17 days stale teaching three retired processes to every session. And it explains check-economics: a check that produces 381 findings and changes roughly six artifacts is a write-only channel too. The corpus's own `feedback-loops-with-consumers` — "Every feedback channel MUST name its consumer and the resulting action" — is the least-cited principle in the whole corpus (4 mentions, against 103 for define-good-up-front). The one principle that would have caught this is the one nobody uses.

**RC2 — The enforcement budget was spent entirely on shape, so every rule about substance is scored by its own author — and the corpus's reflex under correction is to add a recording obligation rather than a mechanism.**
The fault line is perfectly clean and I checked both sides directly. Mechanical constraints hold at 100%: lint PASS 0 violations, `compile_role.py --check` ok on 9 of 9, compile_principles byte-identical, 25 of 25 process skills matching their load point, and the single artifact class inside its word target (rendered role prompts, median 367 against 400) is the only class a compiler produces. Judged constraints are breached at 81–100%: 18 of 18 features over the whole-document target, 25 of 25 process definitions, 18 of 18 decision records, 168 fitness-screen pass cells against 0 fails, `tools-through-skills` at zero artifact_tools references in 25 process definitions against 71 bare sed/grep/awk/cut/head/tail in their own run: blocks, and on 2026-09-17 an agent stamping `status: approved, owner: product-authority` on two role definitions it had just authored because compile_role.py renders nothing else. The lint is the proof: I read its checks and it verifies that a link *resolves*, never that its target is still approved — which is exactly why 31 approved documents cite retired processes and the tool says PASS. When the authority corrected this in 2026-09-05 ("define good up front is supposed to help implementation quality, not just shift the quality responsibility to checks"), the system's response was to add a FIFTH MUST to `define-good-up-front` requiring makers to record their own evaluation — then retire the three processes that held an independent check, leaving bullet 3 ("the check MUST sit with a different role") standing and violated by the two processes that make the primary artifacts. That added obligation is why Document History is 27% of the corpus. The shop has a reflex for adding a rule and none for building a gate.

**RC3 — The corpus has no outward object, so the only thing in reach to govern is itself — and one home-grown clause turns that inward attention into unbounded obligation mass.**
Across 25 process definitions "check" appears 611 times, "user" 0, "customer" 0, "problem" 3; across the whole 160,000-word basis, check 1,231 against user 39 and customer 2. All 18 features and all 16 initiatives target the shop's own definitions or tooling; the one product feature ever framed, progressive disclosure, was parked on day one and its bead has been open 15 days. Structurally the outward path does not exist: no Bounded Context exists on this branch, no contract exists, scenario-assignment's lead-shop-internal path is bead lead-ki66p (open since 2026-09-02, worked around eleven times), and basis/processes/implementation.md plus basis/implementation-principles.md were both authored on day 26 and both stand `draft`. The amplifier is `basis/artifacts/definition.md` §Required sections 2 — "every definition implies at least one check; a definition no check can cite does not govern anything" — inherited by 10 of 24 typedefs and carried as a mandatory screen row in all four principle sets, with no external parent in TOGAF, Spool, Lencioni, Rumelt or BCP 14 and no recorded gap justifying it. Every new definition therefore obliges a new check, every check obliges a recorded evaluation, and with no built artifact to point at, all of it points back at the paperwork. This is why the observed rejection rate is zero (there is nothing to reject but the shop's own documents), why a check that fires on 91% of runs has never returned a feature, and why 0 of 16 initiatives can reach `completed` — the only writer of that state is a process the freeze bars.

The three compound: RC3 gives the system nothing but itself to govern, RC2 means the resulting rules bind nothing, and RC1 means the evidence of both accumulates unread. H1 (verbosity) and H6 (MUST-heaviness) are real and measurable but downstream of all three — and note that the corpus's own verbosity remedy already worked (features 7,562 → 2,836 words) while every factor above still failed. A restart that fixes only the writing reproduces this in 26 days.
input.what_works:
Seven things are genuinely working and are load-bearing. Discarding them is the real risk in a second restart.

**1. The fresh-context cold-reviewer screen — a different role, in a clean context, scoring against a written fitness set.** It is the only check in the system with a detection record: 6 defects, including the three that indict the mechanism competing with it (lead-zddhu on principles.md, lead-fstd0 on architecture-principles.md, lead-u0ow4 on implementation-principles.md 2026-09-17). It also produced the one recorded genuine rejection-and-repair: basis/principles.md v4 history, cold read round 3, "external-standards-first rationale lacked its generic failure example (scenario 3 fail)" → v5 is the forced fix. lead-u0ow4 states the mechanism itself: "the screen table is written by the same agent whose text it scores, in the same pass, and nothing re-derives a claimed pass... The cold-reviewer screen-read step is what actually catches this, every time." Carry this forward and delete the in-document self-screen it was supposed to replace — 168 pass cells and 0 fails, three-for-three unreproducible.

**2. The compilers, and the rule they prove.** compile_role.py, compile_process.py, compile_principles.py, compile_typedef.py, compile_tool.py — part of 4,461 lines of working Python. I ran them: every constraint a compiler enforces holds at 100%, and every always-resident document that has a compiler verified current on the spot. The one always-resident document WITHOUT one is .claude/shop/primer.md, 17 days stale and teaching four retired processes into every session including this one. That contrast is the single most actionable finding in the analysis: **a rule worth having is a rule a compiler can render or refuse; a document worth loading is a document a compiler owns.** Carry the compilers and put the primer under one.

**3. The literal mechanical instruction inside a judged scenario.** basis/fitness/implementation-guidance.fitness.md scenario 6 says "Count the document's words... State the count and pass/fail." Guidance records are the only artifact class near their word target — median 1.1x, 7 of 12 over — against 2.4x–4.3x for every class scored by judgment, because makers actually ran `wc -w`. Same authors, same corpus, same week. Write every criterion as a command that produces a number.

**4. The small-change lane.** 20 of 41 requests routed to it, 28 requests `done`, three changes taken to verified results in about 14 agent-minutes — against roughly four hours and 136 agent-minutes for one full-flow initiative, same agents, same day. The shop diagnosed the reason itself: "no bet, no check of record, one screen only where a definition's own process requires it." This is the working throughput path and it should be the default shape, not the exception.

**5. feat-plain-voice's measured effect — proof the corpus is steerable.** Mean feature size fell from 7,562 words (8 features authored ≤ 2026-09-07) to 2,836 (10 authored ≥ 09-08), with the two most recent at 2,308 and 1,636 — an 85% cut on the extremes. Rendered role prompts came inside their 400-word target (median 367, 7 of 9 compliant), the only compliant class in the corpus. One delivered feature moved a corpus-wide metric. A restart discards that evidence along with the tooling.

**6. The system's honesty about its own failures — the reason this analysis was possible at all.** Every waiver is disclosed in writing: basis/principles.md's own "**The two judged screen rows below claim passes for those principles that the judge could not reproduce.** Accepted, and recorded here rather than silently"; lead-mtq44 disclosing its own maker-stamped approval and citing the precedent; lead-u0ow4 counting itself "Third instance of one class"; feat-execution-vocabulary's three history rows tracking its own word count from 1,250 to 2,800 to 5,000 while failing the same scenario each time. The instrumentation tells the truth even where the enforcement is absent. Most organisations under this much pressure produce comforting records; this one produced accurate ones. That disposition is worth more than any definition in the tree.

**7. Two demonstrated acts of deletion.** product-flow v7 (2026-09-08) removed four process definitions and every human step after the bet; basis/principles.md v12 (2026-09-15) removed a standing principle whole, with the authority's reason recorded verbatim — "There is no mechanism that would be possible to implement in the current system that would meet the principle." Rule-making systems almost never do either. The shop can delete; what it lacks is the sweep that makes a deletion reach the renderings — which is a tooling job, not a discipline job, and therefore fixable.

scores.evidence:
OBSERVED REJECTION RATE ≈ 0 across the whole corpus history. 0 of 18 features carry `status: returned` (grep over features/*.md: 10 assigned, 8 delivered, 0 returned). 0 of 16 initiatives were rejected. I grepped every co-occurrence of a rejection verb (fail|reject|return|blocked|removed) within 120 characters of any of the nine principle slugs across features/, requests/, decisions/, sessions/, initiatives/ and basis/: six hits total, and on inspection NOT ONE is a rejection — they are add-usability run notes (feat-implementation-good.md:151), a designer-criteria row (feat-tool-skills-rest.md:587), two initiative-check attach rows, a PO self-check row, and a 2026-08-23 rationale repair. No check verdict anywhere cites a principle clause as the reason an artifact was turned away.

HYPOTHETICAL REJECTION RATE is also low for most of the set because the obligations are procedural, not discriminating. Against the last ~20 delivered artifacts, `no-orphan-activities`, `single-source-of-truth`, `use-defined-terms` and `governed-context` would reject almost none (all were authored inside a defined process, with one home, using glossary terms). The two that would reject at Spool's two-thirds benchmark are `tools-through-skills` (0 of 25 process definitions reference artifact_tools.py while 71 bare sed/grep/awk/cut/head/tail invocations sit in their own run: blocks — I counted sed 21, cut 20, grep 12, head 10, awk 8, tail 6) and `define-good-up-front`'s different-role clause (feature-authoring runs draft and self-check both as lead-po; adr-authoring runs author and record both as the architect). Both would reject the majority of recent work and rejected none of it.

CONTESTABILITY: ~3 of 9 contested, 6 permission-to-play. Negations no competent shop holds: "activities may sit outside any process", "a fact may have several authoritative homes", "a definition need not be findable", "load context from unapproved sources". Genuinely contested: `tools-through-skills` (many shops prefer bare CLI over a skill wrapper), `least-context` (contested against full-context approaches), `define-good-up-front`'s separate-role check (contested by pair/self-review practice). The corpus's own Lencioni screen row states a position for exactly one column — define-good-up-front, "pass — most systems do NOT work this way"; the other eight read a bare "pass" with no position written.

CHEAP PROXIES: trade-off language across all three sets totals 3 + 4 + 4 instances of "rather than"/"instead of", all incidental clause connectives, none a named accepted cost. Obligations per principle (MUST bullets, counted per heading in basis/principles.md): define-good-up-front 5, tools-through-skills 4, least-context 3, feedback-loops-with-consumers 3, and 2 each for the remaining five — 26 stands under 9 names. Rationales with a concrete failure example: all carry one, but by rule it must be GENERIC.

STRUCTURAL HAZARD CONFIRMED VERBATIM: basis/fitness/principle-set.fitness.md Scenario 3 requires each rationale to "reference no operational history of the product — artifacts, issues, incidents, decision records, or counts." That forbids exactly the evidence Spool's Test #1 demands. No principle in this corpus can prove it came from research, by rule.
scores.counter_evidence: Real and worth stating. (1) The fitness SETS have genuine rejection power even though the principles don't: basis/principles.md v4 history records cold read round 3 returning "external-standards-first rationale lacked its generic failure example (scenario 3 fail)", and v5 is the forced repair — a check that failed something and changed the text. Four screen rounds ran on that one document. (2) The authority exercised rejection power on a principle itself: `delivery-verified` was removed whole on 2026-09-15 with the reason recorded in his words — "There is no mechanism that would be possible to implement in the current system that would meet the principle." A rule in force was deleted, which most rule-making systems never manage. (3) `tools-through-skills` and `single-source-of-truth` did produce filed findings (lead-ng3hc, lead-qd0an, lead-jzmz5) — the principles name defects accurately after the fact, they just never stop anything before it. (4) Complication against a clean zero: the delivery-verified removal was followed two days later by `effect-shown` in basis/implementation-principles.md, near-identical in substance, with no record connecting the two — so even the one clear rejection did not hold.

scores.factor_name: Check economics: does each check pay, and is its verdict reproducible?
scores.evidence:
CHECK MASS IS NOT THE PROBLEM — I counted it myself. 207 steps across 25 process definitions; 25 step ids contain check/screen/verify/judge/review = 12%. 14 of 25 processes have no check step at all. The largest single definition, request-intake (6,562 words, 22 steps), has zero. "Every process ends in a check" is false at the step level.

CHECK COST IS THE PROBLEM. 279 of 592 subagent runs (47%) carry a check/screen/review description and consume 2,173,552 of 5,355,852 subagent output tokens (41%). The authority's own read of init-request-routing: 136 agent-minutes, 66 first implementation, 70 review cycles — 51% of run time — and 20 screen rounds on 8 artifacts. 60 work items ran numbered screen rounds; 32 reached round 3 and 7 reached round 4.

DEFECT FRACTION, JUDGED CHECK: cold-reviewer returned "findings" on 71 of 78 runs and "clean" on 2 — p ≈ 0.91. By Deming's kp that station is worth inspecting. But the output is mostly undecidable: 242 of 381 findings (65%) are "wobbly" — the judge could not decide — and 135 (35%) cite criterion `uncovered`, defined in basis/types/screen-review.md:26 as "for a defect no criterion names." A third of all findings cannot cite the clause they enforce, by design. The shop's own 2026-09-05 analysis: "the cap, not convergence, ended every screen" on seven of eight artifacts, and "the check became where quality is produced."

DEFECT FRACTION, SELF-SCREEN: the opposite extreme and pro forma by construction. I counted the pass cells: 48 in basis/principles.md, 47 in implementation-principles.md, 40 in experience-principles.md, 33 in architecture-principles.md = 168 passes, 0 fail verdicts corpus-wide (the "fail" string hits are prose inside the compile-mapping table, not cells). 100% historical pass rate, asserted by the author in the same pass that wrote the text.

REPRODUCIBILITY — the corpus answers this itself and the answer is 0 of 3. basis/principles.md §Accepted tradeoffs, verbatim: "**The two judged screen rows below claim passes for those principles that the judge could not reproduce.** Accepted, and recorded here rather than silently." Three independent cold screens of three different sets all failed fitness scenario 5 ("every claimed pass is one the judge can reproduce") the same way: lead-zddhu on principles.md, lead-fstd0 on architecture-principles.md, lead-u0ow4 on implementation-principles.md (2026-09-17, filed as "Third instance of one class"). Agreement rate between the author's asserted pass and an independent judge: zero, three for three.

ESCAPE COST: the check has never caught the thing that mattered. 0 of 18 features returned; the P0 that shipped (lead-ibme0 — a feature assigned with an unrecorded decision, silently) was caught by a human reading a line by hand, not by any check step.
scores.counter_evidence: Substantial, and it is the most important counter-evidence in this analysis. (1) THE MECHANICAL CHECKS ARE PERFECTLY REPRODUCIBLE AND ALL PASS. I ran them: `python3 basis/tools/lint_basis.py` → PASS, 0 violations; `compile_role.py --check` → ok on all 9 roles; compile_principles output byte-identical to the compiled block; 25 of 25 process skills match their load point. Every check a machine performs is reproducible; every check a reader performs is not. (2) THE COLD SCREEN IS THE ONE CHECK WITH A REAL DETECTION RECORD — 6 defects, including the three that indict the self-screen it competes with. lead-u0ow4 states the mechanism outright: "the screen table is written by the same agent whose text it scores, in the same pass, and nothing re-derives a claimed pass... The cold-reviewer screen-read step is what actually catches this, every time." (3) A literal mechanical instruction inside a judged scenario converts it into a reproducible check: implementation-guidance fitness scenario 6 says "Count the document's words... State the count and pass/fail", and guidance records are the ONLY artifact class near its word target (median 1.1x, 7/12 over, against 2.4x–4.3x everywhere else) because makers actually ran `wc -w`. (4) The shop already removed three of the four check-shaped processes on 2026-09-08 — it acted on this diagnosis before the authority raised it.

scores.factor_name: Flow efficiency, the single-human constraint, and batch size
scores.evidence:
GOVERNANCE VARIANT IS RED BY A LARGE MARGIN. Of every token the shop's own instrument ever recorded (2,716,421 across 44 rows in 7 files): coordinate/route 64.4%, discovery dialogue 19.6%, MAKE 11.5%, check 4.5%. By role: router 1,247,751 + lead-pm 1,034,027 = 84% to coordination; the three making roles 434,643 = 16%. Time spent satisfying the process about the item exceeds time on the item by roughly five to one.

FLOW EFFICIENCY, 5 items end to end: 13 of the 15 features authored 09-02→09-09 went bet→assigned in 0–1 days — but that measures a markdown corpus editing itself, and the distribution does not survive contact with a build. init-implementation-process was bet 2026-09-09; its two features were authored 09-15 and 09-17 and neither has been built — 8 days open with no closed tail. Git log confirms the stall: 14 commits on 09-09, 1 on 09-10, then five consecutive zero-commit days (09-11 through 09-14), 6 on 09-15.

THE CONSTRAINT IS HANDOFF COUNT, NOT THE HUMAN. Only 10 of 207 steps are human (4.8%), 7 the authority's; product-flow v7 deliberately removed every human step after the bet. Median human turnaround is 6.9 minutes and 18% of his turns are one word. Yet 134 hours of wall-clock waited on the human against 43 hours of agent-active time — 3.11:1, produced by 258 handoffs, not by slow answers. The full flow is "21 agent runs and six human decides to reach one build" (shop's own 09-08 analysis).

THE REAL QUEUE HAS NO SERVER AT ALL. 13 of 41 requests (32%) are stalled — I verified the 7 `routed`-and-never-acted: operational-contract (09-04), step-communication (09-05), migration-review (09-06), messaging-invocations (09-07), initiative-cost-rollup (09-08), cost-per-execution (09-09), artifact-tools-round-trip (09-09). step-communication is named "awaiting the authority's answer" in 8 consecutive session records and is still `routed` today. 36 of 38 correction beads are open; 0 of the 19 filed since 09-06 have closed; 206 pre-rebaseline register items were open on 08-21 and all 206 are still open. Cause verified in the definitions: process definitions contain 8 `bd create`, 11 `bd close`, 3 `bd comment` and ZERO `bd list/show/query`. No defined activity ever reads the register. 28 of 34 open defects wait on nobody — this is an open loop, not a queue.

CLARIFICATION SHARE IS NOT FALLING. Per-initiative cost rose roughly nine-fold (7M cache-read tokens for the first, 64M for each of the last three) across four explicit efficiency interventions. Like-for-like feature-authoring: 192,791 tokens / 8.6 min on 09-09 → 241,852 / 15.4 min on 09-16, same four steps, same roles (+25% tokens, +79% minutes).

BATCH SIZE AND EXTERNAL VALIDATION: the product flow was approved end to end in one batch under brief-032. The interval to external validation is unbounded — no initiative has ever reached `completed` (13 active, 2 planned, 1 proposed, 0 completed), because the only writer of `completed` is reconcile-and-close, which the freeze bars from running. The system cannot observe its own throughput.

AUTHORITY SELF-REPORT — the outcome variable, and it moved the wrong way: cost/speed raised on 11 distinct days starting day 3; 2026-09-07 "We need drastically higher efficiency"; 2026-09-17 "This has been really slow to get moving."
scores.counter_evidence: (1) The small-change lane genuinely achieves flow: 20 of 41 requests routed to it, 28 requests `done`, and three changes taken to verified results in about 14 agent-minutes total — against ~4 hours and 136 agent-minutes for one full-flow initiative. Same agents, same corpus, same day. The shop diagnosed why itself: "no bet, no check of record, one screen only where a definition's own process requires it." (2) The structural move on the constraint was correct: product-flow v7 removed every human step after the bet, and 6 steps carry `asks` as held-and-resumed with defaults rather than as gates. (3) The single-review-cycle ruling of 09-05 did move mean max screen rounds from 2.74 to 2.23. (4) Dollar cost is genuinely not the constraint — a 15-feature product at the unimproved rate is a few hundred dollars of tokens. Steering the system at cost rather than at elapsed time pointed it at its cheapest resource.

scores.factor_name: Ceremonial mass: definitions never executed, rules never retired
scores.evidence:
NEVER-RUN SHARE: 7 of 25 process definitions have no recorded end-to-end execution — corpus-close-out, definition-chain-migration, reconcile-and-close, work-conversation, review-sweep, interaction-conformance-check, implementation. interaction-conformance-check (1,920 words, `status: approved`, rendered to .claude/skills/ and loadable) appears in ZERO session records. That is 28% never-run; but several more are unexecutable by construction while the shop is frozen (implementation, scenario-assignment's dispatch half, reconcile-and-close, the bc-emit and mailbox paths), pushing the unexecutable share past the 40% red flag. product-flow's entire second half has no receiver: no Bounded Context exists on this branch, and scenario-assignment's lead-shop-internal path is bead lead-ki66p, open since 2026-09-02 and worked around eleven times.

DEFINITION-TO-EXECUTION LAG, worst case: basis/processes/implementation.md and basis/implementation-principles.md were both authored 2026-09-17 — day 26 — and both stand `status: draft`. The definition of how to build software arrives on the last day of the window, unapproved, with zero executions. The 4,461 lines of Python that do exist have no tests (`git ls-files | grep -i test` returns nothing).

AUTHORED-AND-KILLED INSIDE 16 DAYS: 8,479 words of process definition (initiative-check 3,548, po-output-check 2,436, stakeholder-presentation 1,476, backlog-ordering 1,019) = 13.5% of the process corpus, retired 2026-09-08.

RETIREMENT WITHOUT SWEEP — the decisive finding, verified by grep. The four retirements happened in the source and nowhere else: po-output-check is still referenced in 19 files, initiative-check in 9, stakeholder-presentation in 8, backlog-ordering in 5. Worst instance: .claude/shop/primer.md, last committed 2026-08-31 (git log confirms — 17 days stale), loaded verbatim into EVERY session, names initiative-check / backlog-ordering / po-output-check as the live product flow and states "deliveries to the authority longer than ~300 words go through the `stakeholder-presentation` process — no exceptions" — a retired process with no replacement. It is in this session's own context. lint_basis.py passes clean over all of it because its link check verifies that a file resolves, never that its target is live. The corpus recorded the consequence: sess-2026-09-16-a, "the stale rendering was teaching the removal's opposite while the removal was being made." A retirement that leaves the compiled context teaching the retired rule is worse than no retirement.

ALSO UNSWEPT: lead-tmahe — backlog-ordering is `status: approved` and its check step routes into po-output-check, which is retired; unnoticed because product-flow no longer calls it at all. An approved process routing into a retired one.

BOZEMAN TEST on the obligations I could trace: I could not find one obligation that PREVENTED a concrete failure in the last 30 days. `single-source-of-truth` and `tools-through-skills` both named defects after they occurred (lead-qd0an — a two-homes breach stale 22 days undetected; lead-ng3hc — six artifact-tool gaps each worked around with sed/grep/cat, "including by the lead-pm role, which is the behaviour tools-through-skills forbids"). Red-tape share on that sample is high: the rules diagnose, they do not stop.
scores.counter_evidence: Genuinely better than the null trajectory on retirement, and this matters for the restart decision. (1) The retirement ratio is NOT zero: four process definitions retired 2026-09-08 in a deliberate flow simplification, and `delivery-verified` — a principle in force — was removed whole from basis/principles.md v12 on 2026-09-15 on the authority's word. March/Schulz/Zhou's expected trajectory is monotonic rule growth; this shop has deleted both a process layer and a standing principle inside 26 days. It CAN retire. What it cannot do is sweep the references. (2) Churn shows rules are genuinely revisited, not silted: 1,217 recorded revisions across 241 versioned documents, mean v5.0, with basis/principles.md at v12, the feature typedef at v18 and the glossary at v27 in 26 days. Rule half-life is days, not years. (3) The rendering machinery correctly REMOVED the retired processes' skills from the agent load point — the compilers swept what they owned. Every stale artifact I found is one no compiler owns.

scores.evidence:
I put each named source's own criteria against the corpus's rendering. Adopted intact: 3. Narrowed, inverted or dropped with NO recorded justification: 7.

TOGAF — five set-level criteria are Understandable, Robust, Complete, Consistent, Stable. All four principle sets render exactly three: "testable (TOGAF... understandable, complete, consistent)" (basis/principles.md:36, architecture:63, implementation:86, experience:69). **Robust and Stable DROPPED** — grep for either across basis/artifacts/principle-set.md, basis/guidelines/principle-set.md and basis/principles.md returns nothing but false positives; no justification recorded anywhere. Worse, **Consistent is INVERTED**: TOGAF's Consistent means the set allows a balance of interpretations without self-contradiction; the corpus folds it into a binary-testability criterion, which removes the balance of interpretations the source criterion exists to protect. ADOPTED INTACT: the Name/Statement/Rationale/Implications form (cited at basis/artifacts/principle-set.md:79) and the 10–20 count heuristic (9 working, 6 each elsewhere).

SPOOL — **Test #1 (comes from research) is INVERTED, in writing.** basis/fitness/principle-set.fitness.md Scenario 3 requires each rationale to "reference no operational history of the product — artifacts, issues, incidents, decision records, or counts." The corpus forbids by rule the only evidence Spool's first test accepts. No recorded justification. Test #2 (helps you say no) adopted in form as a screen row, but scored as the author's own one-line claim. **Test #4 (reversibility) appears only fused into Lencioni's row** via Scenario 6 ("the opposite rule is one an honest shop could adopt") — partially adopted, unattributed, and the remaining Spool tests do not appear.

LENCIONI — four value types (core, aspirational, permission-to-play, accidental). Only permission-to-play survives, as one screen row. Three dropped, unjustified.

BCP 14 — keyword vocabulary adopted by name in five documents and MANDATED by basis/artifacts/principle-set.md:59 ("MUST/SHOULD/MAY per BCP 14 — and is yes/no testable"). **RFC 2119 §6's necessity limit is DROPPED**: grep across all of basis/ for "sparingly" or "only be used where" returns zero hits. §6 says imperatives "MUST only be used where it is actually required... must not be used to try to impose a particular method on implementors" — and "The check MUST sit with a different role holding a different accountability" is precisely a method mandate. The discretion half is unused in practice: 263 MUST + 49 MUST NOT against 10 SHOULD, 0 SHOULD NOT and 26 MAY — 89.6% mandatory, and every SHOULD in the four principle sets is the boilerplate sentence defining the keyword, not a use.

RUMELT — "directs without prescribing method" adopted as a screen row. **The kernel's diagnosis-before-guiding-policy requirement is absent**: no principle set carries a diagnosis section, and Scenario 3's ban on operational history makes one impossible to write.

THE HOME-GROWN CRITERION, flagged hardest as the factor asks: "it implies at least one practice and one check" (basis/principles.md:42, repeated in all four sets and carried as a MANDATORY fitness-screen row). It has NO external parent — it is in none of TOGAF, Spool, Lencioni, Rumelt or BCP 14. And basis/artifacts/definition.md §Required sections 2 makes it structural for every definition in the corpus: "A closing **checks section** (its heading contains 'check') — every definition implies at least one check; a definition no check can cite does not govern anything", inherited by 10 of 24 typedefs. This is the clause that converts a principle set into a generator of process mass, and under the corpus's own `external-standards-first` ("Bespoke structure MUST be justified by a recorded gap in the form it rejects") it required a recorded gap. None exists.
scores.counter_evidence: Real credit due. (1) Every source is NAMED, in every set's Sources line and in the typedef's §Sources, with full citations after the 2026-08-23 close-out polish — most corpora that borrow TOGAF's form do not say so. The departures were findable precisely because the adoptions are declared. (2) One narrowing IS recorded honestly and precisely: Gherkin is adopted as "the readable G/W/T frame — syntax only, no interpreter" in basis/fitness/principle-set.fitness.md §Sources, with the boundary stated rather than assumed. That is exactly the discipline external-standards-first asks for, so the shop knows how to do it. (3) The corpus's own tension between TOGAF (whose principles are guidance) and BCP 14 (whose purpose is removing discretion) is the sharpest fidelity failure, and it is a sophisticated error, not a careless one — it comes from honouring external-standards-first twice without noticing the two standards pull opposite ways.

scores.evidence:
FINDABILITY FAILS ON THE MOST-ASKED QUESTION. "What is the current product flow?" requires reconciling at least three documents at conflicting states: .claude/shop/primer.md (always resident, names three retired processes as the live stages), basis/processes/product-flow.md v7 (current), and the 19/9/8/5 files still citing po-output-check / initiative-check / stakeholder-presentation / backlog-ordering. "Where is the bet taken?" has two live answers: basis/artifacts/initiative.md says "Bet directly at discovery... no separate check between framing and bet"; initiative-check.md still defines step `decide` — "Take the bet" — and is cited by the glossary, the initiative guideline and the initiative fitness set, all approved. "How long may an initiative be?" has two: initiative.md "At most 500 words" vs base-writing-style's target table "Initiative | 400".

STALENESS, MEASURED MECHANICALLY as the factor requires — this is the sharpest number I produced. I ran `compile_typedef.py --check` over all 24 artifact typedefs: **2 pass, 19 will-not-compile ("no `## Writing rules` section" — a section the artifact-typedef typedef declares required), 1 DIVERGED (implementation-guidance: both the guideline the maker reads and the fitness set the checker reads no longer match the typedef they are generated from), 2 refused (superseded/draft).** Only 6 of 30 files in basis/guidelines and basis/fitness carry `generated: true`. And `python3 basis/tools/lint_basis.py` returns "PASS: 0 violation(s)" over every bit of it — I read its checks: frontmatter fields, Document History position, duplicate `defines`, broken links, required headings, $ref sources, request/brief/guidance field shapes. No word count, no currency check, no check that a referenced definition is still approved.

DECODE COST PER SENTENCE rose as length fell: defined-term uses per 1,000 words went request-intake (09-04) 71.9 → product-flow (09-08) 86.7 → implementation (09-17) 94.2 — roughly one defined term every 11 words in the newest definition, against base-writing-style's own 24.3. A writer must hold 120 defined terms (82 glossary + 24 typedefs + 14 data types) and `use-defined-terms` obliges reaching for one wherever one fits.

THE (b)/(c)/(d) SHARE IS THE COST. Document History is 27% of the entire corpus — 1,520 rows, mean 76 words against a 25-word target, max 1,672 words in a single markdown table cell; 69% of all initiative words and 44% of all feature words. Cross-document verbatim repetition (12-word shingles, generated files excluded) is 16.9% of hand-written body words, worst in backlog orders at 54.9% where each day's order restates its predecessor. And 84.5% of a process definition never reaches any agent — 9,145 prompt words of 59,148, with product-flow at 2.7%.
scores.counter_evidence: Two findings genuinely contradict the "dense and unfindable" reading, and I tested both rather than taking them on report. (1) THE GLOSSARY IS HEALTHY. I ran every one of the 82 glossary terms against the whole basis tree, excluding its own definition: only 7 have fewer than 3 uses (simple type, rewrite-forward, conversation type, review record, action table, branched conversation, architecture decision record). 75 of 82 are load-bearing. By the factor's own deletion test, the glossary is in better shape than most production corpora. (2) THE TEXT AGENTS ACTUALLY READ IS THE PLAINEST TEXT IN THE CORPUS. Process step prompts — the only process text that enters an agent's context — measure 22.3 words per unit, 11.8% over 40 words, 31.1% stacking two or more qualifiers: LESS dense on every axis than the typedefs (33.5% stacking), the features (53.2%), or the rendered skills (52.5%). Median sentence length across process definitions is 14 words, typedefs 11, roles 10 — ordinary technical-writing numbers. So the runtime decode cost is low and the maintainer decode cost is high, which inverts the usual causal story: if agents interpret rules inconsistently, prose verbosity is not the channel, because the verbose material never reaches them. (3) The one place density IS extreme is the compilation step, and it is deliberate: 4,053 words of principle carrying 26 obligations become the 537-word always-resident block at one MUST per 21 words, with rationale, implications and screen stripped by design. The corpus solved its verbosity problem by deleting the interpretable half.

data.root_causes:
Three causes explain every failing factor. They are independent; fixing the writing fixes none of them.

**RC1 — Nothing in the system reads what the system writes. Every feedback channel terminates in a write.**
I verified this in the definitions, not just the outcomes: across all 25 process definitions there are 8 `bd create`, 11 `bd close` and 3 `bd comment` calls, and ZERO `bd list/show/query`. No defined activity ever reads the work register. The consequences are the factor scores: 36 of 38 correction beads open, 0 of the 19 filed since 2026-09-06 closed, 206 pre-rebaseline items open on 2026-08-21 and all 206 still open 26 days later; 7 requests `routed` and never acted on, one named "awaiting the authority's answer" in 8 consecutive session records; 7 cost files for 22 sessions with 2 empty including the newest. 28 of 34 open defects wait on nobody — this is not a bottleneck, it is an open loop, and "bottleneck" (H5) is the wrong model for it. The same shape explains ceremonial-mass: retirement happened in the sources on 2026-09-08 and nowhere else, because no activity re-reads the corpus as a whole — hence 19 files still citing po-output-check and a primer 17 days stale teaching three retired processes to every session. And it explains check-economics: a check that produces 381 findings and changes roughly six artifacts is a write-only channel too. The corpus's own `feedback-loops-with-consumers` — "Every feedback channel MUST name its consumer and the resulting action" — is the least-cited principle in the whole corpus (4 mentions, against 103 for define-good-up-front). The one principle that would have caught this is the one nobody uses.

**RC2 — The enforcement budget was spent entirely on shape, so every rule about substance is scored by its own author — and the corpus's reflex under correction is to add a recording obligation rather than a mechanism.**
The fault line is perfectly clean and I checked both sides directly. Mechanical constraints hold at 100%: lint PASS 0 violations, `compile_role.py --check` ok on 9 of 9, compile_principles byte-identical, 25 of 25 process skills matching their load point, and the single artifact class inside its word target (rendered role prompts, median 367 against 400) is the only class a compiler produces. Judged constraints are breached at 81–100%: 18 of 18 features over the whole-document target, 25 of 25 process definitions, 18 of 18 decision records, 168 fitness-screen pass cells against 0 fails, `tools-through-skills` at zero artifact_tools references in 25 process definitions against 71 bare sed/grep/awk/cut/head/tail in their own run: blocks, and on 2026-09-17 an agent stamping `status: approved, owner: product-authority` on two role definitions it had just authored because compile_role.py renders nothing else. The lint is the proof: I read its checks and it verifies that a link *resolves*, never that its target is still approved — which is exactly why 31 approved documents cite retired processes and the tool says PASS. When the authority corrected this in 2026-09-05 ("define good up front is supposed to help implementation quality, not just shift the quality responsibility to checks"), the system's response was to add a FIFTH MUST to `define-good-up-front` requiring makers to record their own evaluation — then retire the three processes that held an independent check, leaving bullet 3 ("the check MUST sit with a different role") standing and violated by the two processes that make the primary artifacts. That added obligation is why Document History is 27% of the corpus. The shop has a reflex for adding a rule and none for building a gate.

**RC3 — The corpus has no outward object, so the only thing in reach to govern is itself — and one home-grown clause turns that inward attention into unbounded obligation mass.**
Across 25 process definitions "check" appears 611 times, "user" 0, "customer" 0, "problem" 3; across the whole 160,000-word basis, check 1,231 against user 39 and customer 2. All 18 features and all 16 initiatives target the shop's own definitions or tooling; the one product feature ever framed, progressive disclosure, was parked on day one and its bead has been open 15 days. Structurally the outward path does not exist: no Bounded Context exists on this branch, no contract exists, scenario-assignment's lead-shop-internal path is bead lead-ki66p (open since 2026-09-02, worked around eleven times), and basis/processes/implementation.md plus basis/implementation-principles.md were both authored on day 26 and both stand `draft`. The amplifier is `basis/artifacts/definition.md` §Required sections 2 — "every definition implies at least one check; a definition no check can cite does not govern anything" — inherited by 10 of 24 typedefs and carried as a mandatory screen row in all four principle sets, with no external parent in TOGAF, Spool, Lencioni, Rumelt or BCP 14 and no recorded gap justifying it. Every new definition therefore obliges a new check, every check obliges a recorded evaluation, and with no built artifact to point at, all of it points back at the paperwork. This is why the observed rejection rate is zero (there is nothing to reject but the shop's own documents), why a check that fires on 91% of runs has never returned a feature, and why 0 of 16 initiatives can reach `completed` — the only writer of that state is a process the freeze bars.

The three compound: RC3 gives the system nothing but itself to govern, RC2 means the resulting rules bind nothing, and RC1 means the evidence of both accumulates unread. H1 (verbosity) and H6 (MUST-heaviness) are real and measurable but downstream of all three — and note that the corpus's own verbosity remedy already worked (features 7,562 → 2,836 words) while every factor above still failed. A restart that fixes only the writing reproduces this in 26 days.
data.what_works:
Seven things are genuinely working and are load-bearing. Discarding them is the real risk in a second restart.

**1. The fresh-context cold-reviewer screen — a different role, in a clean context, scoring against a written fitness set.** It is the only check in the system with a detection record: 6 defects, including the three that indict the mechanism competing with it (lead-zddhu on principles.md, lead-fstd0 on architecture-principles.md, lead-u0ow4 on implementation-principles.md 2026-09-17). It also produced the one recorded genuine rejection-and-repair: basis/principles.md v4 history, cold read round 3, "external-standards-first rationale lacked its generic failure example (scenario 3 fail)" → v5 is the forced fix. lead-u0ow4 states the mechanism itself: "the screen table is written by the same agent whose text it scores, in the same pass, and nothing re-derives a claimed pass... The cold-reviewer screen-read step is what actually catches this, every time." Carry this forward and delete the in-document self-screen it was supposed to replace — 168 pass cells and 0 fails, three-for-three unreproducible.

**2. The compilers, and the rule they prove.** compile_role.py, compile_process.py, compile_principles.py, compile_typedef.py, compile_tool.py — part of 4,461 lines of working Python. I ran them: every constraint a compiler enforces holds at 100%, and every always-resident document that has a compiler verified current on the spot. The one always-resident document WITHOUT one is .claude/shop/primer.md, 17 days stale and teaching four retired processes into every session including this one. That contrast is the single most actionable finding in the analysis: **a rule worth having is a rule a compiler can render or refuse; a document worth loading is a document a compiler owns.** Carry the compilers and put the primer under one.

**3. The literal mechanical instruction inside a judged scenario.** basis/fitness/implementation-guidance.fitness.md scenario 6 says "Count the document's words... State the count and pass/fail." Guidance records are the only artifact class near their word target — median 1.1x, 7 of 12 over — against 2.4x–4.3x for every class scored by judgment, because makers actually ran `wc -w`. Same authors, same corpus, same week. Write every criterion as a command that produces a number.

**4. The small-change lane.** 20 of 41 requests routed to it, 28 requests `done`, three changes taken to verified results in about 14 agent-minutes — against roughly four hours and 136 agent-minutes for one full-flow initiative, same agents, same day. The shop diagnosed the reason itself: "no bet, no check of record, one screen only where a definition's own process requires it." This is the working throughput path and it should be the default shape, not the exception.

**5. feat-plain-voice's measured effect — proof the corpus is steerable.** Mean feature size fell from 7,562 words (8 features authored ≤ 2026-09-07) to 2,836 (10 authored ≥ 09-08), with the two most recent at 2,308 and 1,636 — an 85% cut on the extremes. Rendered role prompts came inside their 400-word target (median 367, 7 of 9 compliant), the only compliant class in the corpus. One delivered feature moved a corpus-wide metric. A restart discards that evidence along with the tooling.

**6. The system's honesty about its own failures — the reason this analysis was possible at all.** Every waiver is disclosed in writing: basis/principles.md's own "**The two judged screen rows below claim passes for those principles that the judge could not reproduce.** Accepted, and recorded here rather than silently"; lead-mtq44 disclosing its own maker-stamped approval and citing the precedent; lead-u0ow4 counting itself "Third instance of one class"; feat-execution-vocabulary's three history rows tracking its own word count from 1,250 to 2,800 to 5,000 while failing the same scenario each time. The instrumentation tells the truth even where the enforcement is absent. Most organisations under this much pressure produce comforting records; this one produced accurate ones. That disposition is worth more than any definition in the tree.

**7. Two demonstrated acts of deletion.** product-flow v7 (2026-09-08) removed four process definitions and every human step after the bet; basis/principles.md v12 (2026-09-15) removed a standing principle whole, with the authority's reason recorded verbatim — "There is no mechanism that would be possible to implement in the current system that would meet the principle." Rule-making systems almost never do either. The shop can delete; what it lacks is the sweep that makes a deletion reach the renderings — which is a tooling job, not a discipline job, and therefore fixable.
